common_name: Rothschild's Slipper Orchid (King of the Paphiopedilums)

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded greenhouse specimen in bright, indirect light in a coarse, fast-draining terrestrial orchid mix; give this Borneo native intermediate-to-warm temperatures year-round and avoid letting the mix stay soggy.

directions: Pot in a chunky bark-and-perlite mix that drains within seconds of watering, since the thick roots rot quickly in stagnant moisture. Provide steady warmth, high humidity, and bright filtered light rather than direct sun to encourage the long, horizontally held petals that give this species its 'Kinabalu gold' nickname. Mature clumps take several years to reach blooming size but reward patience with one of the largest flowers in the genus, often carrying two to four blooms per stem. Feed lightly and consistently through the growing season rather than with occasional heavy doses, and repot only when the mix breaks down.
sources: American Orchid Society - Paphiopedilum Culture Sheet
Kew Science, Plants of the World Online - Paphiopedilum rothschildianum
Royal Horticultural Society - Paphiopedilum Growing Guide

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in a fine-bark terrestrial orchid mix with added perlite for sharp drainage; this Vietnamese species prefers slightly warmer, drier conditions than most mottled-leaf slipper orchids.

directions: Use a small pot with a fine, fast-draining bark mix, since the compact root system of this species does poorly in oversized containers that stay wet. Its softly mottled leaves and pale pink, rounded flowers make it a favorite parent for pastel-colored complex hybrids, but the species itself is prized for its delicate coloring and compact habit. Allow the mix to approach dryness between waterings and reduce watering slightly in winter to mimic its native dry-season rest. Keep humidity moderate to high but ensure good air movement to prevent crown rot in the tightly clustered growths.
sources: American Orchid Society - Paphiopedilum Culture Sheet
Kew Science, Plants of the World Online - Paphiopedilum delenatii
Orchid Species Culture Notes, International Phalaenopsis Alliance

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in a fine-bark terrestrial orchid mix; give this Himalayan-foothill species cooler winter nights than most Paphiopedilum to trigger reliable autumn flowering.

directions: Pot in a small container with a fine bark mix and keep roots consistently but lightly moist, letting the surface dry slightly between waterings. This species is instantly recognizable by its upswept, twisted lateral petals and boldly veined, upturned pouch, a shape unlike any other commonly grown slipper orchid. Cooler nighttime temperatures in autumn help set the flower spikes, so avoid overly warm year-round conditions typical of lowland tropical growers. Provide bright but indirect light and moderate humidity, and divide congested clumps only when they have several mature growths to spare.
sources: American Orchid Society - Paphiopedilum Culture Sheet
Kew Science, Plants of the World Online - Paphiopedilum fairrieanum
Royal Horticultural Society - Paphiopedilum Growing Guide

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in a fine-bark terrestrial orchid mix; this Myanmar-region species tolerates slightly cooler, drier conditions than many lowland Paphiopedilum.

directions: Grow in a compact pot with a fine, well-drained bark mix, since the fibrous roots resent being oversized in a container. The wide, rounded, rosy-pink dorsal sepal held above narrow downswept petals is the species' hallmark and a common influence in pastel hybrid breeding. Native to limestone cliffs, it appreciates slightly drier roots between waterings and a bit more calcium in the mix than average, achieved by including a few crushed oyster-shell or dolomite chips. Keep humidity moderate and provide good air circulation to prevent the compact growths from rotting at the base.
sources: American Orchid Society - Paphiopedilum Culture Sheet

planting.note: Mount bare-root on a slab or grow unpotted in a slatted basket with no potting medium, hung in bright, filtered-to-nearly-full light; this India and Sri Lanka native tolerates more sun and drier air between waterings than many Vanda hybrids.

directions: Hang the bare roots in a slatted basket or wire cage so they can dry within an hour or two of each watering, misting or soaking daily during warm weather and less often in cooler months. Its yellow-green, brown-checkered flowers are lightly fragrant and appear on arching spikes from the leaf axils, typically in spring. This species tolerates brighter light and lower humidity than many other Vanda, making it a good choice for a sunnier windowsill or bright patio. Fertilize weekly at quarter strength during active growth and flush the roots with plain water periodically to prevent salt buildup.
sources: American Orchid Society - Vanda Culture Sheet
Kew Science, Plants of the World Online - Vanda tessellata
Royal Horticultural Society - Vanda Growing Guide

planting.note: Mount bare-root on a slab or grow unpotted in a slatted basket with no potting medium, hung outdoors or on a bright patio in filtered-to-full sun; this vigorous hybrid flowers nearly year-round in warm, humid climates.

directions: Grow bare-root in a hanging slatted basket with the long roots free to drape and dry between frequent waterings, providing bright light with some protection from the harshest midday sun. Bred in Singapore in the 1890s from Vanda teres and Vanda hookeriana, this sterile hybrid produces sprays of vivid magenta-pink, long-lasting blooms almost continuously in warm, humid, sunny conditions. Because it lacks a true pseudobulb and stores little water, keep the roots from drying out completely for extended periods, especially during hot weather. Feed regularly at diluted strength and give the sprawling, vining stem sturdy support as it climbs and lengthens over the years.
sources: National Parks Board Singapore - Vanda Miss Joaquim, National Flower of Singapore
American Orchid Society - Vanda Culture Sheet
Singapore Botanic Gardens - History of Vanda Miss Joaquim

planting.note: Mount bare-root on a slab or grow unpotted in a small slatted basket with no potting medium, in bright, filtered light; this Himalayan-foothill species prefers noticeably cooler winter nights than most tropical-lowland Vanda.

directions: Mount on a small slab or hang in a miniature slatted basket so the compact root system dries quickly after each watering. Unlike the large, flat-flowered tropical Vanda hybrids, this species is a compact, cool-growing miniature from the Himalayan foothills, bearing waxy yellow-green flowers marked with maroon-brown at the lip in short axillary clusters. Give it a distinct cooler, drier winter rest with reduced watering to mimic its native seasonal cycle and encourage flowering. Provide bright light and good air movement, since its small size makes it more prone to rot in stagnant, overly humid conditions than larger Vanda species.
sources: American Orchid Society - Vanda Culture Sheet
